chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Sufyan ibn Ayyinah, from Al-Zuhri who said: I heard Ali ibn Al-Hussein (peace be upon them) say:

Whoever is not consoled by the consolation of God, his soul will be cut off from the world with regrets, and by God, this world and the Hereafter are but like the two pans of a scale; whichever side outweighs, it takes the other with it,
When the Event comes to pass, There is no denying its coming,
meaning the Resurrection, It will cast down, It will raise up, God will cast down by it the enemies of God into the Fire, and God will raise up by it the friends of God into Paradise.

Then he turned to one of his companions and said to him: Fear God and be concise in your seeking, and do not seek what has not been created, for whoever seeks what has not been created, his soul will be cut off with regrets and he will not attain what he sought.
Then he said: And how can one attain what has not been created? The man said: And how can what has not been created be sought?

He said: Whoever seeks wealth, possessions, and abundance in the world, he is only seeking that for comfort, and comfort was not created in the world nor for the people of the world. Indeed, comfort was created in Paradise and for the people of Paradise, and toil and hardship were created in the world and for the people of the world,

and whoever is given a skin-bag (of wealth) from it, is given double the greed for it; and whoever acquires more of the world, is more needy in it, because he needs people to protect his wealth, and needs every tool of the world. Thus, there is no comfort in the wealth of the world,
but Satan whispers to the son of Adam that he has comfort in collecting that wealth. And he is led to toil in the world and reckoning for it in the Hereafter.
Then he (peace be upon him) said: No, the friends of God do not toil in the world for the world, but they toil in the world for the Hereafter.

Then he said: Indeed, whoever worries about his sustenance, a sin is recorded for him. Thus said the Messiah [Jesus] (peace be upon him) to the disciples: This world is a bridge, so pass over it and do not build on it.

key_terms.كَفَّتَيْ الْمِيزَانِ: The two pans of the scale

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between worldly wealth and true comfort according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali ibn al-Hussein (Zayn al-Abidin) elucidates the metaphysical balance between the transient world and the eternal Hereafter, emphasizing that true comfort (Rahat) is exclusively reserved for Paradise, while toil is inherent to worldly life. He warns that excessive pursuit of wealth leads to spiritual poverty and increased dependency, reinforcing the Shia concept of prioritizing the Hereafter over worldly accumulation. The Imam supports this by citing the Quranic description of the Day of Judgment as a scale that lowers the enemies of God and raises His friends, urging believers to traverse the world like a bridge without dwelling in it.
